history.summary: DISAMBIGUATION FLAG: this is a local Shiva temple in Pali city, Rajasthan - NOT the Somnath Jyotirlinga of Prabhas Patan, Gujarat. It stands in the main market / Suraj Pole area (Nadi Mohalla) of Pali, district Pali, Rajasthan; CSV town 'Pali' is correct. Per Rajasthan travel sources, the shrine was built by the Gujarat king Kumarpal Solanki in '1209' - reported as Vikram Samvat 1209, which equals 1152-53 CE, though some sites write 1209 AD; the era ambiguity is flagged. Raj Kumar Pal Solanki is said to have brought the Shiva Linga from the Saurashtra region of Gujarat and installed it here. The shrine is known for its shilp (stone-carving) art: intricate carvings on the shikhara and pinnacle, circular ceiling patterns, and inside the sanctum a Shivalinga with idols of Parvati, Ganesha and Nandi, plus a smaller shrine in the complex. CAUTION - travel sites repeat the claim that 'Mahmud of Ghazni attacked this temple many times'; Mahmud's famous raids targeted the Gujarat Somnath (1025-26 CE), which predates this temple by over a century on any dating, so the claim is likely a conflation - flagged as verify. No CSV correction needed: town Pali, district Pali, state Rajasthan are correct.

name: Somnath Temple
town_description: Pali is an industrial and trading city in Rajasthan's Marwar region, on the banks of the Bandi river. The Somnath Mandir stands in the main market area near Suraj Pole, about 2.6 km from the Pali bus stand.

travel.airport: Jodhpur Airport is the nearest airport (~75 km).
travel.railway: Pali Railway Station (~2.2 km) connects to Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur, Ahmedabad and other major cities.
travel.road: Located in the centre of Pali city near Suraj Pole; easily reached by bus or taxi; Pali Bus Stand is about 750 m away.

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter season, per local guides).
